text.p: L-Bank, or Landeskreditbank Baden-Wuerttemberg, could launch a five-year mark Eurobond soon, syndicate managers said on Monday.
Issue size was likely to be between 750 million marks and one billion marks, they added.
"Many triple-A rated borrowers are looking at the five-year sector now because the arbitrage is good," a Frankfurt-based syndicate manager said.
"L-Bank is most likely to come first, though," he added.
A launch spread of around 20 basis points over German government bonds was likely, traders said.
One dealer said Dresdner Bank had already been mandated to lead the issue, but an official there declined to comment.
Earlier on Monday, Bayerische Vereinsbank announced plans for a one billion mark five-year Pfandbrief bond, which could be launched on Tuesday.
A spread of 30 b.p. over the Obl 119 was expected.
Traders said an L-Bank deal might not come until Wednesday to avoid clashing with the BayerVB issue.
"Although Pfandbrief are domestic bonds, they do have an international appeal. Borrowers will need to consider that when they launch straight Eurobonds," a trader said.
